text:
lev: Quick idea: move "slowpath requeue" out of upstreams and into the edge. Edge would detect long stalls in streaming (configurable threshold, e.g. 350ms) and attempt a single in-flight switch to another healthy backend while keeping client TCP/stream open. RFC stub: https://redwood.internal/rfc/edge-midflight-switch (WIP).

sonya: main worry = duplicates & side effects. If a write already happened upstream then requeue could replay. We need a dedupe contract.

miguel: we already have x-rw-id but it's optional. For streaming users often don't include it. Could auto-assign a requeue id at edge and send it to upstreams. Upstreams opt-in to honour dedupe for N seconds.

lev: proto: edge sets header `x-rw-requeue: <uuid>` and also emits a small lease blob in control-plane for 2s. On requeue, new upstream gets client prefix and header. Upstream returns 200 normally or 409+`x-rw-requeue-dupe:true` if it detects duplicate.

sonya: how about ordering? client expects byte-for-byte continuity. When we switch the new backend's KV is cold -> will generate extra latency and might produce truncated/overlapping tokens.

miguel: KV warmup strategies: 1) disallow requeue for model backends that require expensive KV warmup, 2) edge shadow-warm candidate by sending prefix to a warmed replica (costly), 3) quick fallback: hedge to multiple backends but keep first-complete wins.

infra: storing per-inflight requeue state at edge increases memory churn. Keep it tiny: store only uuid + 8 byte origin reference + expiry. Also GC aggressively.

anna: telemetry: counters/events needed: `edge.requeue.attempt`, `edge.requeue.success`, `edge.requeue.dup_detected`, `edge.requeue.fallback_to_client_close`. Sample full traces when a requeue occurs.

sre: Ops rules: cap to 1 requeue per request, global per-instance budget, and alert if requeue.fallback > 0.5% over 5m. Also watch token burn when shadow-warm is enabled.

lev: safety net: requeue feature behind flag `edge.midflight_requeue`. Phase 0: internal endpoints only and only idempotent paths. Phase 1: opt-in upstreams that advertise cheap warmup. Phase 2: broader experimental rollout.

miguel: compatibility contract: include a tiny table in the RFC mapping model families -> requeue policy (forced-off, warmed-only, hedged). eng-runtime please add model KV cost tags.

dev-bot: Feature flag `edge.midflight_requeue` created (off).

eng-runtime: also consider a 'requeue-probe' mode: when threshold breaches, edge forks a lightweight probe (no token billing) to candidate to check KV readiness before switching. That reduces wasted tokens but increases control-plane complexity.

lev: good point. I'll add state machine: IDLE -> STALLED -> PROBING -> SWITCH -> FINALIZE/FAIL. Will include header contract, TTLs, dedupe semantics, and trace example.

sonya: don't forget to document failures: what the client sees for each outcome (stream continues uninterrupted, stream restarts, or client gets 5xx). We need predictable surface for SDKs.

anna: SDKs should surface `requeue.attempted` and `requeue.outcome` in diagnostics logs. Add sampling policy for traces (always sample requeue traces).

lev: I'll draft the RFC with experiments: small canary on internal traffic, synthetic load tests for KV-warmup heatmap, and chaos tests that kill upstreams midstream. Will ping infra & sre for perf numbers.

miguel: one final: consider API-level opt-out header `x-rw-requeue: none` clients can set to opt-out. Useful for customers who already handle dedupe.

lev: thanks. RFC by EOD tomorrow. @infra @sre @eng-runtime please review.
